description: Calculate resolution for print. Pass print `width` and `height` with `unit` (mm, cm, in), optional `viewing_distance` with `distance_unit` (cm, in, m) and optionally `pixels_w`, `pixels_h` of the image you have. Formulas: pixels = size in inches x ppi; the ppi a viewer can resolve at distance d is 1 / (2 d tan(0.5 arcminute)) which is about 3438 / d(inches), assuming normal 20/20 vision resolves 1 arcminute; effective ppi = pixels / size in inches. Returns pixels needed at the acuity-suggested ppi (capped at 300) and at 300 ppi, and, if you give pixel dimensions, the effective ppi and a verdict. 300 ppi is the usual figure for work held in the hand; large format is viewed from farther away and can go lower. The vendor's stated minimum wins. 'DPI' here means image pixels per inch.

pixels_w.description: Image width in pixels you have
